chunks: A case comes before one of them regarding a ruling from the rulings, so he judges in it according to his opinion. Then that same case comes before another, so he judges in it contrary to his statement. Then the judges gather together at that time with their Imam who appointed them, and he validates all their opinions, although their God is One! And their Prophet is one! And their Book is one!
ai.seo_question: Why do Islamic jurists issue contradictory verdicts for the same case according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) critiques the reliance on subjective reasoning (ra'y) in early Islamic jurisprudence, highlighting the irony that contradictory verdicts are mutually validated by a unified religious authority. This passage underscores the Shia emphasis on the necessity of a single, authoritative source of truth—ultimately pointing to the Imams—to resolve such discrepancies among scholars who share the same divine foundation.
